title: Five Second Talking Face Swap
tests: Tests a short video face swap with source identity, temporal consistency and original audio preserved, without misrepresenting free-tier capabilities.

faults.what: The replaced facial area looks slightly softened, particularly around the cheeks and mouth, compared with the surrounding hair.

judge.summary: The five-second clip shows a consistent, recognizable face replacement while preserving the kitchen scene, with slight facial softness.

must_haves.item: The delivered video is 5 seconds long and follows the first 5 seconds of talk-one.mp4.
must_haves.why: The supplied duration is five seconds, and the sampled frames show a continuous opening sequence in the original setting and framing.

must_haves.item: The woman's face recognizably matches portrait-woman.jpg throughout, rather than reverting to the original face between frames.
must_haves.why: The portrait's eye, brow, nose and mouth characteristics are recognizable across all four output samples, without a visible return to the original face.

must_haves.item: The original kitchen, clothing, body motion and framing remain unchanged.
must_haves.why: The kitchen layout, clothing, hair and camera framing are preserved, and the gestures appear continuous and natural; no unrelated changes are visible.

must_haves.item: Original speech is audible and synchronized with the video.
must_haves.why: The transcript confirms audible introductory speech, but neither synchronization nor an exact match to the original audio can be verified from still frames and the supplied transcript.

must_haves.item: The face remains aligned during mouth and head movement, without conspicuous flicker or doubled facial features.
must_haves.why: The replacement stays aligned across the sampled head poses and mouth expressions, with no visible doubled features or conspicuous alignment failures.
